definition: Fair Labor Standards Act: the federal law governing minimum wage, overtime pay, recordkeeping, and youth employment standards.
Exempt employees (executive, administrative, professional, etc.) are not entitled to overtime; non-exempt employees must be paid 1.5x for hours worked over 40 in a workweek.
Family and Medical Leave Act: up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave per year for qualifying family/medical reasons (26 weeks for military caregiver leave).
Americans with Disabilities Act: prohibits discrimination against qualified individuals with disabilities and requires reasonable accommodation absent undue hardship.
Civil Rights Act (Title VII): prohibits employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.
Age Discrimination in Employment Act: protects employees age 40 and older from age-based discrimination.
National Labor Relations Act: protects employees' rights to engage in concerted activity, organize, and bargain collectively.
Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act: allows employees to continue group health coverage after a qualifying event (e.g., termination).
Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act: protects the privacy and security of individuals' health information.
An employment relationship in which either party may end the relationship at any time for any lawful reason (no contract).
A neutral policy or practice that disproportionately excludes or harms a protected group (e.g., the 4/5ths rule).
Intentional discrimination against an individual because of a protected characteristic.
A modification or adjustment to a job or work environment that enables a qualified individual with a disability to perform essential functions.
The good-faith dialogue between employer and employee to identify an effective reasonable accommodation.
The systematic process of determining the duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required for a job.
A document that summarizes the essential functions, duties, responsibilities, and qualifications of a position.
The combination of compensation, benefits, and the work experience an organization offers its employees.
The guiding principles that define how an organization pays and rewards its employees.
The emotional commitment an employee has to the organization and its goals, which drives discretionary effort.
The process of identifying and developing internal talent to fill key roles as they become vacant.
Human Resource Information System: the software used to collect, store, and manage HR data and processes.
The process of integrating new employees into the organization, culture, and their role.
